groups.name: Playable roster
groups.note: The 21 playable animals (C01–C21 of 07-devonian-design.md). All have delivered models; this board is for authoring a canonical pose per animal and then correcting the model against it. Lengths are the representative and maximum real lengths from docs/research/devonian-swimming.json, not game units.

subjects.name: Dunkleosteus terrelli
subjects.role: C01 · Rung IV giant · the jaws that cut through armour
subjects.imagesAre: Most Commons material is the old long-bodied reconstruction. The shipped body follows Engelman's short, deep trunk (fineness 2.7–3.2); judge the pose against that, not against the museum silhouette.

subjects.name: Titanichthys
subjects.role: C02 · Rung IV giant · the toothless gape, a filter feeder

subjects.name: Coccosteus cuspidatus
subjects.role: C03 · Rung II · the small arthrodire, armour in front and a flexible tail

subjects.name: Bothriolepis canadensis
subjects.role: C04 · Rung II · the boxy antiarch with jointed armoured arms

subjects.name: Gemuendina stuertzi
subjects.role: C05 · Rung II · the flattened ray-shaped placoderm that buries itself

subjects.name: Doryaspis nathorsti
subjects.role: C06 · Rung II · the jawless shield with a long oral projection

subjects.name: Cladoselache fyleri
subjects.role: C07 · Rung III · the first shark shape, the fastest straight line

subjects.name: Stethacanthus
subjects.role: C08 · Rung III · the anvil brush on its back, a bluff
subjects.imagesAre: Most illustrated Stethacanthus material is Carboniferous (S. altonensis). The roster entry is a Late Devonian representative of the same symmoriiform grade.

subjects.name: Cheirolepis trailli
subjects.role: C09 · Rung II · the shoaling ray-fin, everyfish
subjects.imagesAre: Cheirolepis is also a fossil conifer genus (Cheirolepidiaceae). Searching the species keeps the fish; anything leafy on this board is the plant.

subjects.name: Rhinodipterus kimberleyensis
subjects.role: C10 · Rung II · the lungfish that breathes air
subjects.imagesAre: Very little of Rhinodipterus on Commons. Expect a thin board; other Gogo dipnoans are the nearest comparison and are not this genus.

subjects.name: Onychodus jandemarrai
subjects.role: C11 · Rung III · the tusk whorls, the largest hunter

subjects.name: Tiktaalik roseae
subjects.role: C12 · Rung III · the neck and the weight-bearing fins, the shallows ambusher

subjects.name: Acanthostega gunnari
subjects.role: C13 · Rung II · eight fingers, an aquatic early tetrapod

subjects.name: Eldredgeops rana
subjects.role: C14 · Rung I · the schizochroal eyes, and a shell that enrolls
subjects.imagesAre: Most specimens on Commons are filed under the older name Phacops rana and will not reach this board. If it comes back thin, search Phacops rana by hand — it is the same animal.

subjects.name: Walliserops trifurcatus
subjects.role: C15 · Rung I · the trident nobody can explain
subjects.imagesAre: Moroccan trilobite material on Commons includes restored and composite specimens. Prefer museum-credited images for the trident's real proportions.

subjects.name: Jaekelopterus rhenaniae
subjects.role: C16 · Rung III · the largest sea scorpion, claws first

subjects.name: Nahecaris stuertzi
subjects.role: C17 · Rung I · the phyllocarid scavenger, first to the corpse

subjects.name: Furcaster palaeozoicus
subjects.role: C18 · Rung I · the brittle star, five arms and no hurry

subjects.name: Palaeoisopus problematicus
subjects.role: C19 · Rung I · the sea spider that swims

subjects.name: Manticoceras
subjects.role: C20 · Rung I · the coiled goniatite that hangs in the water
subjects.imagesAre: The shell is well known; the soft body is not preserved. Anything with tentacles on this board is interpretation.

subjects.name: Michelinoceras
subjects.role: C21 · Rung II · the straight shell that swims backwards
subjects.imagesAre: Orthocone shells are common on Commons; Michelinoceras by name is not. Soft body and resting trim are unconstrained.

groups.name: Attached organisms and shell props
groups.note: B01–B12 of the design brief, shipped as 20 prop GLBs in public/assets/devonian/props/. One subject per family; the -v2 variants are the same organism and share this board. These are model requests, not animals.

subjects.name: Stromatoporoid massive dome
subjects.role: B01 · The reef's dome-builder · Clathrodictyon-type sponge
subjects.imagesAre: Stromatoporoids are sponges, not stromatolites — reject anything filed as a microbial mat. Most files are cut sections and weathered domes; the living surface is interpretation.

subjects.name: Amphipora branching stromatoporoid
subjects.role: B02 · Slender branching sponge thickets

subjects.name: Stromatoporoid encrusting growth
subjects.role: B03 · Thin layered growth over whatever it sits on

subjects.name: Favosites
subjects.role: B04 · Honeycomb tabulate colony

subjects.name: Striatopora branching tabulate coral
subjects.role: B05 · Delicate branching skeletal framework
subjects.imagesAre: Striatopora is thinly represented. Thamnopora and Cladopora are the same Devonian branching growth form and will not reach this board by name — search them by hand if it comes back empty.

subjects.name: Heliophyllum solitary rugose coral
subjects.role: B06 · The horn coral · skeleton and living oral surface

subjects.name: Hexagonaria colonial rugose coral
subjects.role: B07 · Connected corallites in a Devonian colony
subjects.imagesAre: Much of what Commons holds is polished Petoskey stone: the same coral, cut and polished, not a living surface.

subjects.name: Crinoid stalked camerate
subjects.role: B08 · Stem, attachment, cup and feeding arms

subjects.name: Mucrospirifer brachiopod bed
subjects.role: B09 · Ribbed lampshells on the floor · not generic clams

subjects.name: Fenestella fenestrate bryozoan
subjects.role: B10 · Lace colony of repeated zooids

subjects.name: Platyceras gastropod shells
subjects.role: B11 · Small coiled shells, mostly empty

subjects.name: Modiomorpha bivalves
subjects.role: B12 · Paired valves and hinge, Devonian outlines
subjects.imagesAre: Modiomorpha is thinly covered on Commons. Any Devonian bivalve slab is a fair comparison for outline and hinge; a modern clam is not.

groups.name: Plants and algae
groups.note: P01–P05. These do not all belong together: marine algae, early terrestrial vegetation and later forest trees are separate collections with separate regional tags.

subjects.name: Rhynia gwynne-vaughanii
subjects.role: P01 · Leafless branching axes · the Rhynie chert plant, not shoreline grass

subjects.name: Asteroxylon mackiei
subjects.role: P02 · Early lycophyte · do not enlarge it into a later giant lycopsid

subjects.name: Wattieza cladoxylopsid tree
subjects.role: P03 · Devonian tree architecture · not a palm and not a tree fern
subjects.imagesAre: Commons has little of the whole tree. The Gilboa stumps, filed as Eospermatopteris, are the same plant's base and will not reach this board by name.

subjects.name: Archaeopteris
subjects.role: P04 · The late Devonian woody tree · a spore-bearer, not a flowering tree

subjects.name: Devonian marine algal thalli
subjects.role: P05 · Sheet, tuft and branching thalli · no kelp forest, no seagrass
subjects.imagesAre: Fossil Devonian algae are barely represented. This board is deliberately broad — anything with a modern kelp or seagrass silhouette is the wrong evidence.

groups.name: Geological and organic props
groups.note: G01–G12. Named for material and form rather than for their role in the game. G08, G09 and G12 are derived from approved shell, crinoid and creature anatomy rather than generic bones and shells.

subjects.name: Limestone carbonate outcrop
subjects.role: G01 · Low slab, mound and vertical face · submerged weathering

subjects.name: Reef framework limestone
subjects.role: G02 · Buttress, overhang and low shelf of the reef itself

subjects.name: Limestone rubble fragments
subjects.role: G03 · Angular and rounded fragments · exposed interiors

subjects.name: Mud fine sediment bed
subjects.role: G04 · Low-relief rippled and smooth mud · material-driven detail

subjects.name: Sand and pebble bed
subjects.role: G05 · Two grain mixes and scattered stones

subjects.name: Bank erosion at a channel margin
subjects.role: G06 · Sloped bank, undercut and exposed face · the unrooted version

subjects.name: Boulder weathered silicate
subjects.role: G07 · The rock slot · grain and mineral vary by region

subjects.name: Coquina shell hash
subjects.role: G08 · Broken shell fragments · not a field of giant valves

subjects.name: Crinoid columnal debris
subjects.role: G09 · Disarticulated stem pieces · millimetres, not boulders

subjects.name: Callixylon submerged log
subjects.role: G10 · Intact, broken and part-buried timber · Archaeopteris wood

subjects.name: Archaeopteris root-bearing bank
subjects.role: G11 · Roots in a bank face · no generic mangrove prop

subjects.name: Dunkleosteus gnathal plates
subjects.role: G12 · Disarticulated remains · the era's carrion prop

groups.name: Regional environments
groups.note: E01–E09. Nine separate reference environments, not nine neighbouring zones of one place. A fossil deposit is not a living surface: pyritised Hunsrück slabs and desert-weathered Moroccan exposures are burial and later erosion, not the sea these animals lived in.

subjects.name: Hunsrück Slate marine shelf
subjects.role: E01 · Early Devonian mud shelf · Gemuendina, Nahecaris, Furcaster, Palaeoisopus
subjects.imagesAre: Almost everything on Commons is a pyritised fossil slab or a slate quarry. The animals were not metallic gold and the seabed was not quarried slate.

subjects.name: Morocco Devonian shelf
subjects.role: E02 · The Walliserops-bearing carbonate shelf
subjects.imagesAre: Modern desert exposure of Devonian rock does not establish a desert shoreline in the original marine setting.

subjects.name: Orcadian Basin lake
subjects.role: E03 · Middle Devonian lake · Coccosteus and Cheirolepis

subjects.name: Gogo Formation reef
subjects.role: E04 · Late Devonian reef system · Onychodus and Rhinodipterus

subjects.name: Miguasha National Park
subjects.role: E05 · Late Devonian waterway · Bothriolepis and Cheirolepis

subjects.name: Cleveland Shale offshore sea
subjects.role: E06 · Latest Devonian offshore sea · Dunkleosteus and Cladoselache · not a coral garden

subjects.name: Ellesmere Island Devonian channel
subjects.role: E07 · Broad shallow channel with submerged timber · Tiktaalik
subjects.imagesAre: Commons has modern Arctic Ellesmere landscapes, not the Fram Formation setting. Useful for water and bank structure only.

subjects.name: Greenland Devonian floodplain
subjects.role: E08 · Acanthostega's shallow water body · its own sediment and vegetation
subjects.imagesAre: Nothing on Commons shows the Britta Dal Formation as a living place; expect modern East Greenland landscape and outcrop.

subjects.name: Svalbard Old Red Sandstone
subjects.role: E09 · Early Devonian water bodies · Doryaspis · distinct from the later wooded settings
